RESOLUTION NO. 2026 075
A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN BRUNO SUBMITTING TO
THE VOTERS AT THE NOVEMBER 3, 2026 GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION A MEASURE
THAT PROPOSES ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE REPEALING INITIATIVE ORDINANCE
NO. 1284 RELATING TO VOTER APPROVAL TO PERMIT BUILDINGS EXCEEDING THREE
STORIES OR FIFTY FEET IN HEIGHT, ANY INCREASE IN RESIDENTIAL UNITS OR
OCCUPANCY IN RESIDENTIAL ZONING DISTRICTS IN EXCESS OF LIMITS PERMITTED ON
OCTOBER 10, 1974, MULTISTORY PARKING STRUCTURES, AND DEVELOPMENT-THAT
ENCROACHES UPON, MODIFIES, WIDENS OR REALIGNS CRYSTAL SPRINGS ROAD
BETWEEN OAK AVENUE AND JUNIPERO SERRA FREEWAY, AND SNEATH LANE FROM
EL CAMINO REAL TO THE WESTERLY CITY LIMITS; REQUESTING THAT SUCH ELECTION
BE CONSOLIDATED WITH THE STATEWIDE GENERAL ELECTION HELD ON THAT DATE;
TAKING CERTAIN OTHER ACTIONS; AND FINDING SUCH ACTION EXEMPT FROM CEQA
WHEREAS, by prior resolution, the City Council called a general municipal election (the
"Election") for November 3, 2026, to be consolidated with the statewide general election to be
held on that same date;
WHEREAS, the City Council desires to have the matter of an ordinance that would
repeal Initiative Ordinance No. 1284, an initiative measure to require an affirmative vote of the
voters of the City of San Bruno prior to any City approvals that allow: (i) buildings exceeding
three stories or fifty feet in height, (ii) any increase in residential units or occupancy in residential
zoning districts in excess of limits permitted on October 10, 1974, (iii) multistory parking
structures, and (iv) development that encroaches upon, modifies, widens or realigns Crystal
Springs Road between Oak Avenue and Junipero Serra Freeway, and Sneath lane from El
Camino Real to the westerly City limits; be presented to the voters on the November 3, 2026
ballot; and
WHEREAS, since the adoption of Ordinance No. 1284, the California Legislature has
enacted a broad array of State housing laws that override local zoning regulations, including
voter-approved height and density limits, reducing the City's local control over land use
decisions and such that many of the development scenarios the Ordinance was designed to
subject to voter approval may now proceed under State law regardless of local voter sentiment;
and
WHEREAS, State law, including but not limited to the State Density Bonus Law, SB 9
(2021), and SB 79 (2025), has significantly pre-empted the housing-related provisions of
Ordinance No. 1284, further eroding local control over residential development while the
Ordinance continues to impose meaningful constraints on commercial and economic
development; and
WHEREAS, the practical effect of Ordinance No. 1284 on San Bruno's economic
development goals has been documented, including the loss of the Crossings Hotel
development opportunity in 1999 and the decision by a major employer to redirect campus
expansion plans to other jurisdictions due in part to the constraints imposed by the Ordinance,
representing significant foregone property tax, business license tax, and transient occupancy
tax revenue; and
WHEREAS, the City Council has established strengthening the City's fiscal base and
attracting private investment as core economic development goals, including through the
Elevate San Bruno initiative launched in January 2026, which seeks to make San Bruno more
competitive through updates to the General Plan, Specific Plans, and Municipal Code; and
WHEREAS, adoption of this Resolution and approval of this ballot measure would
modify only the approval process for such developments and projects, with any future proposal
for a development or project remaining subject to all applicable General Plan policies, zoning
and development standards, discretionary review requirements, and environmental review
under California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA").
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN
BRUNO, CALIFORNIA, AS FOLLOWS:
Pursuant to Election Code Sections 9222 and 10201, the City Council directs that the
ordinance attached hereto as Exhibit "A" and incorporated herein by reference (the
"Measure') be submitted to the qualified voters of the City of San Bruno at the Eiection.
The question shall appear on the ballot as follows:
Shall City of San Bruno Ordinance No. 1284, the 1977 zoning initiative that
requires voter approval before the City Council can approve buildings
exceeding specified height limits, residential density increases beyond
1974 zoning, multi-story parking structures, and certain roadway changes,
be repealed given that State housing laws supersede local height limits and
the ordinance interacts with current City economic development goals?
Yes
No
The Measure shall only take effect if at least a majority of those voting on the question
vote in favor of it at the Election.
The full text of the Measure, attached to this Resolution as Exhibit A, being the proposed
ordinance repealing Initiative Ordinance No. 1284, shall be completely printed in the
voter pamphlet.
The City Council hereby directs the City Clerk to transmit a copy of the Measure to the
City Attorney. The City Attorney shall prepare an impartial analysis of the Measure, not
to exceed 500 words in length, showing the effect of the Measure on the existing law
and the operation of the measure, and transmit such impartial analysis to the City Clerk
no tater than August 18, 2026 by 5:00 p.m.
Pursuant to Elections Code Section 10403, the City Council requests that the San Mateo
County Board of Supervisors consent to consolidation of the election for the Measure
with the general election to be conducted by the San Mateo County Registrar of voters
on November 3, 2026. The election shall be held in all respects as if there were only
one election, and only one form of ballot shall be used. The election will be held and
conducted in accordanée with the provisions of law regulating a special election
consolidated with a statewide election. The City will bear all costs customarily charged
by the County to a city in connection with a ballot question submitted at a municipal
election that is consolidated with an election conducted by the County.
The City Council directs the City Clerk to file a certified copy of this Resolution with the
Registrar of Voters of San Mateo County.
Notice of the time and place of holding of the election is given and the City Clerk is
authorized, instructed, and directed to give further or additional notice of the election in
the time, form, and manner as required by law.
Pursuant to Section 10400 et seq. of the Elections Code, the Board of Supervisors of
San Mateo County is requested to consolidate the election on this ballot measure with
other elections held on the same day in the County.
10. The Board of Supervisors is authorized to canvass the returns of the Election pursuant
to Section 10411 of the Elections Code.
11. Pursuant to Section 10002 of the Elections Code, the Board of Supervisors is requested
to permit the County Clerk to render all services specified by Section 10418 of the
Elections Code relating to the election, for which services the City agrees to reimburse
the County, in accordance with current County pro-rations and allocation procedures.
12. The City Clerk shall file a certified copy of this Resolution with the Clerk of the County
Board of Supervisors.
13. The City Clerk is hereby authorized to do all things necessary and proper to implement
the provisions of this Resolution.
14. This Measure is exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15061 (b)(3)
because it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that this ballot measure
will have a significant effect on the environment. Adoption of this Resolution and
approval of this ballot measure would modify only the approval process for certain
development projects, but any future proposal for such development projects would
remain subject to all applicable General Plan policies, zoning and development
standards, discretionary review requirements, and environmental review under CEQA.
Therefore, approval of the ballot measure would not result in a direct or reasonably
foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment.

Proposed Ordinance
AN ORDINANCE OF THE PEOPLE OF THE CITY OF SAN BRUNO, CALIFORNIA TO
REPEAL INITIATIVE ORDINANCE NO. 1284 CODIFIED IN CHAPTER 12.26 OF THE
SAN BRUNO MUNICIPAL CODE
THE PEOPLE OF CITY OF SAN BRUNO ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:
SECTION 1. The purpose of this Ordinanceis to repeal Initiative Ordinance No. 1284, an
initiative measure to require an affirmative vote of the voters of the City of San Bruno prior to
City approvals that allow buildings exceeding three stories or fifty feet in height, any increase in
residential units or occupancy in residential zoning districts in excess of limits permitted on
October 10, 1974, multi-story parking structures, and development that encroaches upon,
modifies, widens or realigns Crystal Springs Road between Oak Avenue and Junipero Serra
Freeway, and Sneath Lane from El Camino Real to the westerly City limits.
SECTION 2. Chapter 12.26 of the San Bruno Municipal Code is hereby repealed in its entirety.
SECTION 3. If any provision, clause, sentence or paragraph of this Ordinance or the
application thereof to any person or circumstance shall be held invalid, such invalidity shall not
affect the other provisions of this Ordinance which can be given effect without the invalid
provisions or application, and to this end the provision of this Ordinance are declared to be
severable.
SECTION 4. This ordinance shall take effect 10 days after the City Council declares the results
of the vote at the November 3, 2026, election.
Approved by the People of the City of San Bruno at the General Municipal Election Held
on November 3, 2026.
Rico E. Medina
Mayor
